summary: Darius sets 120 satraps and three presidents Daniel one of them because excellent spirit, intends set him over whole realm, other presidents seek to find occasion against Daniel concerning kingdom but can find no fault, say we shall not find occasion except concerning law of his God. They counsel king to make decree 30 days no man ask petition of any god or man except king or be cast into den of lions, king signs. Daniel knew decree signed, goes home windows open toward Jerusalem, kneels three times a day prays gives thanks as formerly. Men assemble find Daniel praying, tell king Daniel disregards decree, law of Medes Persians no revoking, king sore displeased sets heart to deliver Daniel labors till sundown, men say king no decree can be changed, king commands Daniel brought cast into den, stone laid on mouth sealed. King passes night fasting, early morning goes to den cries with lamentable voice Daniel servant of living God, has your God been able to deliver? Daniel says O king live forever, my God sent angel shut lions' mouths because innocency found in me and before you I did no hurt. King exceeding glad, commands take Daniel up no manner of hurt found because believed in God. King commands those men who accused Daniel, their children wives cast into den lions overpower and break bones before touching bottom. Darius writes to all peoples nations languages peace be multiplied, I make decree men tremble and fear before God of Daniel for he is living God steadfast forever.
whyItMatters: Daniel in lions' den — deliverance, accusers punished, Gentile king's decree that all tremble before Daniel's God. Shows praying despite decree, God shuts mouths of lions, innocency and faith.

keyVerses.text: When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.
keyVerses.why: Disobedience to decree, obedience to habit — windows open toward Jerusalem, three times daily.

questions.question: Why does law of Medes and Persians not be revoked matter?
questions.answer: Verse 8,12,15 says law of Medes and Persians cannot be revoked, even king cannot change. Historical claim: Persian law unchangeable, giving plot device — king wants to save Daniel but cannot, must obey own law. Irony: king's unchangeable law vs Daniel's unchangeable habit of prayer. Shows human law unchangeable forces injustice, but God's law of mercy overrides. Later Esther also has unrevokable law, needs second decree to counter.

questions.question: Why does Daniel pray with windows open toward Jerusalem three times a day knowing decree?
questions.answer: Windows open toward Jerusalem — direction of prayer toward temple (Solomon's prayer 1 Kings 8:48-49 pray toward place). Three times daily — perhaps morning noon evening (Psalm 55:17 evening morning noon). He does as formerly — habit, not defiant show, but doesn't hide either. Knowing writing signed, he still goes home windows open prays. Civil disobedience by continuing faithful practice, not provoking but not compromising. For readers facing pressure to hide faith, model of open consistent prayer.

questions.question: What does 'my God sent angel shut lions' mouths' mean and why families of accusers also thrown?
questions.answer: Angel shut mouths — like angel in furnace earlier, presence protecting. Because innocency found in me before him and before you I did no hurt — Daniel claims innocence before God and king, trusted God so believed. No hurt found because believed in God (v23). Then king commands accusers, children and wives cast into den and lions break bones before bottom — harsh retributive justice, Persian practice of family punishment, shows reversal, but also troubling to modern reader — collective punishment. Narrative's focus is deliverance and Gentile king's decree that all tremble before living God.
